newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FIGURE SKATING-RUSSIANS "TAKE ON WORLD" IN CANADA.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-RUSSIANS "TAKE ON WORLD" IN CANADA.

text.p: It will be Russia against the rest of the world at the final Champions' Series event in Hamilton this weekend, the head of the Russian Figure Skating Federation predicted as his team flew off to Canada on Tuesday.
"It'll be a virtual two-team contest -- Russia versus the world," said Valentin Piseyev.

The Russians, who skated off with all four golds at the European Championships in Paris last month, are in fine form which they hope can carry them through to the World Championships in Lausanne next month.

European singles champions Irina Slutskaya and Alexei Urmanov will be joined by pairs gold medallists Marina Yeltsova and Andrei Bushkov, though ice dance champions Oksana Gritshuk and Yevgeny Platov were not named in the squad for Hamilton.
The event runs from Friday to Monday.
Anzhelika Krylova and Oleg Ovsyannikov and Irina Lobacheva and Ilya Averbukh will take part in the dance.
Olga Markova, Maria Butyrskaya, Ilya Kulik and Alexei Yagudin will also skate in the singles and the pairs team also includes Oksana Kazakova and Artur Dmitriyev.
